page.overview:
What is Arthurian legend?

Arthurian legend, named for its key figure Arthur, is a blanket term for hundreds of tales of knights, ladies, squires, quests, wars, and supernatural figures.

The Arthurian story has been told and retold for centuries, being innovated or expanded in almost every rendition. Because of this, the Arthurian legends are a dynamic collection of tales which are adapted to be meaningful to each passing generation, rather than being one set story.

Whether Arthur was originally a Celtic folk hero, a real person or the imaginings of an unknown bard, he became a central figure in British history and culture. His story has been adopted by different cultures in Britain and travelled across continents, with each version of the legend being moulded to fit the people and culture who adopted it.

This article is a chronological journey through the key periods in the development of Arthurian legend, and with it, an insight into how historical changes, shifts in power and religion along with different cultural attitudes have shaped the legends we know today.
